newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe hospitals cut patient admissions.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe hospitals cut patient admissions.

text.p: Two of Zimbabwe's largest hospitals have cut patient admissions because of a staff shortage after some doctors and nurses workers were dismissed for striking last year, a hospital official said on Monday.

According to a statement by Yasin Ali, medical superintendent at Harare Central Hospital, hospitals have suffered acute staff shortages since the government fired 10,000 nurses and junior doctors who went on strike in October over pay.
Some of the nurses and doctors were reinstated in December.

"We are currently experiencing an acute shortage of nursing staff resulting from the dismissals last month...It is clear that the immediate replacement of these posts is impossible," the statement said.

"We have agreed that the hospital in-patients be reduced by 20 percent of the normal hospital bed capacity (i.e. 20 percent reduction for each normal ward capacity) to enable the limited number of nurses to manage," Ali said.
Harare Central hospital normally has a nursing staff of 847 and around 1,400 patients in its wards at any time.
